title: Native ports: games as plain Rust programs

units.title: Design the native port: a game as a plain Rust program
units.detail: june 2026-10-31 (d/modded-builds-are-plain-rust-programs-no-save): a modded build is literally a Rust program: no registers, no GBA memory block, no CPU, nothing preserved for save states or rewind; as regular and pretty as we can make it. Write docs/native-port-design.md covering: (1) where game state lives (globals as typed statics or one Game struct, from DWARF types where a decomp has them; a byte array only where types aren't known yet); (2) the hardware as a library, not memory (the runtime's PPU and sound behind an API like ppu.bg[0].scroll_x, the CPU gone; prior art: the SM64 and OoT PC ports' renderers); (3) the frame loop that replaces the main loop's V-blank wait, and interrupt handlers as callbacks; (4) function pointers as Rust fn values, and as IDs with a lookup table where the game does arithmetic on them (Emerald splits them into halves in task data); (5) ROM addresses as analysis-time facts only: return-address tricks like WarioWare's sub lr, lr, #24 resolved to a fixed destination at lift time (docs/research/code-without-rom-addresses.md); (6) holes: anything not statically resolved (undiscovered code, unresolved indirect jumps, RAM code, untyped pointer arithmetic) is a build error or a listed hole, since there's no interpreter fallback; (7) the oracle: the native program draws the same frames as the play build from the same inputs (the play build and its exact checks become the native port's oracle); (8) data pointers, DMA and struct copies, and what each needs. Read the existing analysis, structured codegen and mod-view designs first; cite the code. Propose the units that follow. Stop at ~3 h.

record.evidence: docs/native-port-design.md covers the card's 8 points with code citations and proposes 8 units (5 new filed). units.title: Spike: one of our agb programs as a native Rust program
units.detail: Take one of our own agb programs (agb/, our own source: small, no legal issues; one with a frame loop, input and a background or sprites, e.g. agb/template or agb/windows-blend) and lift it all the way to a native Rust program per docs/native-port-design.md: no Machine, no registers, no GBA memory map; state in Rust types, the hardware through the library API, a frame loop. Done when it draws the same frames as its play build (exact recompiled build) for the same input script over a few hundred frames, the code is committed, and the doc records what was hard, what was done by hand that the lifter should do, and what the next units should be. Stop at ~4 h with what's measured. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): no agb/ program reads input, so first write a new agb/native-spike (agb source only; D-pad moves a sprite and scrolls a background; SCENE.md). The native program lives in its own crate (crates/native-spike or agb/native-spike-native, your call) and takes the desktop's flags: --headless --frames N --input <script> --frame-hashes F. Done when: native and the exact play build give identical --frame-hashes files over 600 frames of a script that moves something at least every 60 frames, and one planted wrong store makes them differ.

Findings: docs/research/native-agb-spike.md. Branch t3/a5d53ea7, unmerged.

units.title: Hole report: what blocks a native build of each game
units.detail: A tool (Rust, not bash) that lists, for a ROM, everything that blocks a pure native build per docs/native-port-design.md's hole list: code reached in runs or fuzzing that discovery didn't find; indirect jumps and calls not resolved; return-address arithmetic (the scrambled-return-address side-by-side tool from docs/research/code-without-rom-addresses.md finds it, e.g. WarioWare's IWRAM helper); code run from RAM; pointer arithmetic or casts the known types don't explain, where types exist. Run it on the eight games of that research (Emerald, Kirby, Metroid Zero Mission, Minish Cap, WarioWare, moonbeam and the rest) and write each game's counts and worst holes into docs/research/native-holes.md, ranked by how close each game is to native. Propose discovery or fuzzing units aimed at the commonest holes. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): put the hard-hole classification in the analysis crate (the lifter reuses it). Runs: the research doc's 5,400-frame press script through the interpreter's coverage, for all eight ROMs listed by file name. Untyped pointer arithmetic: report 'not measured until stage B'. Rank by hard holes, then bytes reached but not discovered. Done when native-holes.md's counts match the tool's output on all eight, and the controls hold: WarioWare's 0x3000468 lr-24 helper listed as a hole, moonbeam's __gnu_thumb1_case_* resolved, Emerald's unresolved-jump count equals Recovery's.

record.evidence: just holes on all eight ROMs (5,400 frames, research press script): each first line identical to docs/research/native-holes.md's ranking lines (Metroid 18, WarioWare 22, moonbeam 23, Kirby AM 29, Kirby NiDL 30, Emerald 34, Minish Cap 46, Rogue 86). Controls: WarioWare 0x03000468 site-24 listed NOT resolved; moonbeam __gnu_thumb1_case_uqi/uhi (0x08042e00/14) resolved; Emerald 11 unresolved = Recovery's 670-659 (just discover). Classification in analysis::holes, cargo test -p analysis holes 10 passed. Review: fresh subagent, 11 findings fixed or documented (b251fd00). just check, disc-pret, disc-agb, jt-score pass.

units.title: Emerald: ten functions as native Rust, scored against pret
units.detail: Like {unit:mod/decomp-spike}, but native per docs/native-port-design.md: ten Emerald functions of varied shape (a leaf getter, an array loop, a call chain, a switch, struct field access, u8/u16 arithmetic, one that stores a function pointer; ClearBattleMonForms and SeedRngAndSetTrainerId among them) lifted to plain Rust over typed state from pret's DWARF, with no registers, Machine or addresses. Emerald is the measuring stick, not the goal: score each against pret's C (statements, named accesses, loop shapes, anything left raw), and say what the lifter needs for each gap. Check behaviour where it can be: the same results as the play build's function on the same inputs (fn-diff style). Write side-by-sides and scores into docs/native-port-design.md. Never copy pret's C text into the repo ({d:mod-view-prints-pret-s-file-line-never-pret-s-c}). Stop at ~3 h. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): mirror-safe (decision): lifted code and side-by-sides go in mods/emerald/native-ten/ (left out of the public mirror); docs/native-port-design.md gets only scores and gaps. The ten: {unit:mod/decomp-spike}'s eight (mods/emerald/decomp-spike/) plus CalcCRC16 and GetBgAttribute; reuse its scoring columns. Behaviour check: a native form of fn-diff (entry state as guest-layout RAM + params from {unit:native/summaries}; compare RAM, I/O, return value, ignoring stack below sp). Done when it prints 'native 0 of 10 differ' and a one-byte edit gets caught.

record.evidence: just native-ten: 'native 0 of 10 differ' (3,072 runs), ROM-byte fault under Random caught 671/672; verifier's own one-byte edits (CalcCRC16 0x8408->0x8409, GetBgType arm) caught; 19 hand edits caught. Review by fresh subagent: 6 findings fixed (8372fdfe). just check passes.

No bar (decision: measure only): the tool prints agree/disagree/no-proto counts and per-category disagreement counts, 10 per category checked by hand, numbers quoted in the design doc. A unit test where a function clobbers r4 fails its proof.

units.title: Lift report metrics and a bars file the lift check holds
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md, 'How every piece is checked' and piece 0. Shared code every stage-B unit needs. (1) gbaa-lift writes its metrics into report.txt as `name value` lines, split by region so later bars mean something: lines of src/main.rs; functions lifted, recognised, replaced, unrecognised; functions with a summary hole; four-register functions without a summary hole; byte loads/stores at a constant address per region (RAM, I/O, ROM, VRAM/palette/OAM); at a computed address per region where the value set says, else unknown; sp-relative loads/stores; call_fn calls; jumps by value; stand-ins; gap targets (codegen::native's count() today lumps these). (2) `--bars FILE` fails the lift when any metric is over its bar (maxima only; a unit that needs a relation adds a metric whose bar is 0), naming it. (3) The program list moves out of the lift-check recipe into the same committed TOML (one table per program: ROM, route, flags, bars) read by a Rust driver (a gbaa-lift or route-check mode), so later units add a program by adding a table, not bash ({d:stage-b-checks-are-bars-in-one-committed-file}). Bars start at today's values; only lowered. Done when: just lift-check runs from the TOML and passes; a codegen test lowers one bar below the measured value and the lift fails naming that metric; the planted store and planted hard hole are still caught; just check passes.

units.title: Fallthrough into another function keeps r4-r11 and flags
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md, piece 1. Stage A prints a fall (or jump) into another function's entry as a tail call, so the continuation starts with r4-r11 and NZCV zeroed (codegen::native goto/call_then). Real agbcc games do this. units.title: A pending IRQ is taken the moment IME is set again
units.detail: Found by {unit:native/lift-irq-hold}, written up in docs/native-stage-b.md. agb's critical_section, and agbcc games, mask by clearing IME rather than the I bit; on the hardware a pending IRQ is taken the moment IME is written back to 1. Both the play build at --timing native and the hardware library take it at the next wait instead. They agree with each other, so the native check can't see it; only mGBA can. Write a small agb test program (source only, like agb/native-irq-hold) that clears IME across V-blank and reads its frame count before and after setting IME again; fix the hardware library and tick_native so an IME write releases held IRQs, like hw::irq_release for the I bit. Keep the old behaviour behind a gbaa-lift flag as a planted_flags control. Done when: the test program's route matches mGBA's hash (just mgba-diff) on both the play build at --timing native and the exact interpreter; just lift-check passes with the program added and the flag's control caught; just check passes.

record.evidence: Verifier (fresh context) reran: just mgba-diff native-ime-release 601 matches mGBA (abc7ac7a22ed22b3); gbaa-desktop --timing native same hash (old play build drew 0346a4614af57b13); just lift-check (all 7 programs, after merging main) passed with --ime-at-waits caught at frame 2 EWRAM 0x020000cc; just check passed; diff review found no bugs. lines_prelude 500->508: IME_RELEASE const+doc and io_write16's IME case.

units.title: Function flow: callees' values kept apart by call site
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md piece 3. Measured by {unit:native/fnref-heap-sites} (its branch, commit 0868fc7e, splits the pile into frame and allocation-site objects): fn_words_not_proven doesn't move on any agb program, even with the pile dropped altogether. The run joins every caller's r0-r3 and sp at a callee's entry, and every call_fn set is all ~21 address-taken functions, so a shared function's pointer parameters (memcpy, fmt, qrcodegen's encoders) reach dozens of frames, anywhere in each, and one read through them gives every function address stored in any. Give the run call-site context (a callee's entry and results per call site, or per caller, for callees small or shared enough; k=1 to start), on top of the object split. Done when: fn_words_not_proven falls on every agb program (bars lowered to the measured values), a unit test where two callers pass one callee two objects and the callee's read of the first gives only what the first caller stored, just lift-check and just check pass.

Write each as a stand-in (Rust f64 mul/div, bit-exact on the soft-float's results), found by its code the way analysis::flash recognises routines, so every game with them gets it. Done when: gbaa-holes counts none of them hard on moonbeam and Rogue (the report must learn the stand-ins), a test pins the f64 results against the interpreter on edge cases (denormals, NaN, inf, rounding), just check passes.

units.title: Kirby Nightmare lifts with no hard holes and builds
units.detail: gbaa-lift on Nightmare (--name kirby-nightmare, a holes file with only skip_fn_flow; without it the fn flow hits 16G: {unit:native/whole-lift-memory}) ran in 1 min, 474M peak, 2026-11-07: 4899 functions, 15 hard holes. Write mods/kirby-nightmare/holes.toml as mods/metroid/holes.toml does: skip_fn_flow; stand-ins for the reset 0x08000000 (2 msr) and the IWRAM IRQ wrapper f_03001030 (mrs 0x03001040, 0x030010b4, msr 0x030010c0); targets for the jump at 0x0800474e (the run, holes/coverage/kirby-nightmare-in-dream-land.toml). The 9 BIOS calls (swi 0x00 0x01 0x0a 0x0c 0x11 0x12 0x13 0x25 0x28 in the stubs at 0x080cfa50-0x080cfa92) wait on {unit:native/lift-bios-calls}. Done when: the lift exits 0 and its crate builds in release under just long; lines, build time and peak RAM quoted in docs/native-stage-b.md; just check passes.

units.title: Lifted task switchers run tasks on host coroutines
units.detail: Shared code for {unit:native/nightmare-task-switch} (docs/research/native-holes.md, 'Kirby: Nightmare's task switcher'). The lifter doesn't count a stack switch (mov sp, rN; ldr sp, [rN]) as a hard hole: on Nightmare it lifts 0x08000244/0x08000278/0x08000298 silently, though gbaa-holes counts them. Make it hard there too, and give stand-ins a prelude facility: run a task's lifted code on a stackful coroutine (corosensei, as crates/desktop/src/coro.rs; the generated crate's Cargo.toml gains it), keyed by the guest sp it saved; resume starts or resumes, yield/exit suspend with the values the scheduler reads. Test it on an agb program with a small ARM switcher of that shape (resume, yield with a frame count, exit) and 3+ tasks, as a lift-check case with a stand-in and a planted control. Done when: lift-check green with the case, its bars set; just check passes.

units.title: Discover code past m4a's and Nightmare's copy sources
units.detail: {unit:native/kirby-undiscovered} left two kinds of ROM code inside a BIOS copy's source undiscovered on purpose (docs/research/native-holes.md, What discovery misses): m4a's SoundMainRAM copy ends in the bx r3 stub SoundMain calls in ROM, hiding SoundMain's tail (38 bytes, every m4a game), and Nightmare's crt0 copy runs into its coroutine switch at 0x08000234, entered by a veneer's ARM b (36 bytes, and 44 after calls into it). Extending discovery::copy_cuts to them (stub targets, b targets) finds it but each game's hard count rises by the jumps found there: SoundMain's constant jump into its IWRAM copy (needs a holes-file entry in the lift) and the switch's bx r1. Decide whether a constant jump to a discovered overlay entry should be resolved (Recovery and the lifter's dyn_targets) so it isn't a hole, then extend the cut. Done when: those bytes are discovered in just holes-all --against main, no hard count higher (or the rise explained and agreed), disc-* bars hold, just check passes.

units.detail: On main at aa63a25 (2026-11-07), just holes-all --only kirby-nightmare --cover fails: holes/coverage/kirby-nightmare-in-dream-land.toml lists 13 jumps (0x080cdeac, 0x080ce4a0 and others) that are no longer unresolved, resolved by units since. units.title: Function flow: loads through unknown addresses
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md piece 3. Measured on {unit:native/fnref-context}'s branch (commit e81168f; it holds the object split and call-site context): fn_words_not_proven unmoved by either. ~640 of affine's load sites (spike 644) have an address that may be unknown (Val::unk), and each reads the pile and every RAM cell (Run::load_at's anywhere arm), so e.g. the IRQ vector word's f_03000000 is in nearly every hole. Not the cause (tried, no change): naming the allocator, dropping the pile from constant-address loads, dropping the I/O unk flag, NUMS 8->256. A seen source: main's inlined free-list walk at 0x080001a8 (affine) loads GLOBAL_ALLOC fields holding allocator-made pointers. Find where the unknown comes from (GBAA_FNREF_TRACE; print each anywhere load) and fix the first big source. Done when: fn_words_not_proven falls on every agb program, bars lowered, a unit test, just lift-check and just check pass.
